street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (FY ends April; FY2026 is actual; FY2030 EBITDA 645.1M on revenue 3,522.5M)

evidence_of_progress.note: Q4 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 21.8% vs 22.4% (VA quarterly actuals, -57 bps). Q1 FY2027 CFO said '$53 million or 11% of revenue' vs 12.4% in Q1 FY2026 (-140 bps); the CEO in the same call said 'nearly $46 million', so the Q1 figure needs checking against the 8-K. FY2027 guide of $305M to $325M implies flat margin; ramp is back-end loaded to FY2028 to FY2030.

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: FY2030 consensus adjusted EBITDA margin is 18.3%, inside management's 18% to 20% range and only 69 bps below the midpoint. Forward EBITDA consensus was also cut 18.3% over 12 months, which reads as a broken near-term story rather than an unproven one. Separately, a March 2026 goodwill restatement and material weakness (8-K 0001104659-26-076140) is a governance flag.
verdict: Catalyst and numeric framing match GXO, but the street already models the low end of the FY2030 18% to 20% target and has cut EBITDA 18%, so the gap is missing; not a GXO setup.
open_questions: Which Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA figure is right ($46M or $53M) and does the second-half two-thirds EBITDA weighting hold?
Is the FY2030 margin recovery mostly a return to legacy AV's pre-merger 18% via mix, and how much depends on LOCUST and SCAR timing?
Did the restatement and material weakness change board composition or controls beyond the Arlington director exits?
